newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks trade lower on political worries.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks trade lower on political worries.

text.p: Delhi stocks traded lower in early trade on Friday on slackness in buying linked to a corruption scandal involving a ruling party leader, brokers said.

They said worries over the federal police's decision to prosecute the chief minister of the state of Bihar, Laloo Prasad Yadav, in the scandal involving illegal diversion of animal welfare funds, hit the market.
Yadav, who is the president of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party, says he is innocent but has refused to accept opposition demands that he must step down and face trial.
The benchmark index dropped 1.19 points at 800.05 in the first 30 minutes of trading.
The Janata Dal is a leading member of the ruling United Front coalition.
"The return of pro-market Finance Minister P.Chidambaram failed to have any positive impact on the sentiment," said Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.
Chidambaram was sworn in on Thursday after his regional party decided to join Gujral's government formed on April 21.
Reliance Industries dropped 2.0 rupees to 306.50 and TISCO 1.20 to 183.50 rupees.
